set.body:
Goal: train one scale per aesthetic per plot over the union of all layer data, replacing per-layer scale training. This is the one real soundness hole.

Evidence: ScalePhase.registry builds a registry from each layer env (CompilerPhases.scala:46-48, PlotCompiler.scala:212); AesEnv.bind only blocks duplicate scales within a single env (AesEnv.scala:27-32); each layer maps its rows into its own [0,1] (Scales.scala:468-475); the panel range unions the per-layer [0,1] ranges (CompilerPhases.scala:395-402); the derived axis comes from firstScale (CompilerPhases.scala:613-617, used at :501). So two layers carrying different continuous x-scales (different domains) each rescale into [0,1], the panel unions them, and the axis is taken from layer one only — layer two marks are positioned on an axis that lies about them. MixedPositionScaling (CompilerPhases.scala:392-403) catches scaled+unscaled but not scaled+differently-scaled.

Acceptance: a plot-level scale registry trained over the union of all layers before geom lowering; one scale per aesthetic per plot (ggplot2 invariant); differently-scaled layers either share the trained scale or produce a typed error, never a silently wrong axis; callers may still supply an explicit scale but it trains plot-wide; conformance gains a two-layer differing-domain case; parity note against ggplot2 scale-union; JVM+JS tests. Ergonomic win: callers stop hand-training per layer.
set.title: Graphics: plot-global scale training (fix the scale-coherence hole)
